blurb: Sleek Siamese-type cat in hundreds of colors, usually with green eyes
description: The Oriental Shorthair is a cat breed developed in the US and UK from the Siamese: medium-sized, slender and muscular, in many colors, and social and vocal.
answer: The Oriental Shorthair is a domestic cat breed developed from, and closely related to, the Siamese, keeping its slender body and wedge-shaped head but in a wide range of colors and patterns. It is a medium-sized cat, usually green-eyed, commonly described as social, curious and talkative.

body: The breed's roots lie in landrace cats from Siam (Thailand), many of which were full-colored rather than pointed. When Siamese were selectively bred from the late 1800s, the pointed cats became Siamese and the others were called non-blue-eyed Siamese or foreign shorthairs. In the early 1970s, New York-area breeders led by Vicky and Peter Markstein took up solid and tabby cats of Siamese type, based on cats bred by Baroness von Ullmann in the 1950s. The CFA accepted the Oriental Shorthair for championship in 1977 and the GCCF recognized it in 1997.

Orientals have almond-shaped eyes, a wedge-shaped head with large ears, and a sleek but muscular body. They are medium-sized: males average about 3.5 to 5.5 kg, with females under 3.5 kg. More than 300 color and pattern combinations are theoretically possible, including solid, tabby, smoke, shaded, tortoiseshell and bicolor, though permitted colors vary by registry. The Oriental Longhair differs only in coat length.

The personality is commonly described as very similar to the Siamese. Breeders and veterinarians describe Orientals as active, curious, social, intelligent and often vocal. Many stay playful into adulthood and enjoy fetch, and they are said to prefer living in pairs or groups and to seek human interaction.

Orientals are described as athletic, with high activity levels and an ability to leap into high places, so play and climbing opportunities suit them. Sources give little detail on grooming for the short coat.
The source material names no breed-specific health conditions. The listed lifespan is about 17 years. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: What is the difference between an Oriental Shorthair and a Siamese?
faq.a: The Oriental keeps the modern Siamese body and head but comes in a wide range of colors and patterns instead of only points, and is usually green-eyed rather than blue-eyed.
Yes. Like the Siamese, they are commonly described as natural conversationalists, and many are quite vocal.

faq.q: How big does an Oriental Shorthair get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat; males average about 3.5 to 5.5 kg and females under 3.5 kg.
